title: Decomposition and structure diagrams
starter: You have been asked to organise a charity bake sale. Write down every separate job it involves, then group them.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: What decomposition is
facts: Decomposition means breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems.
You keep splitting until each part is small enough to solve on its own.
The parts become subprograms, modules or separate jobs for different people.
stations.challenge: Break 'run a school sports day' into five sub-problems.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Decomposition means breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems.
Also credit: You keep splitting until each part is small enough to solve on its own.

questions.a: Breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems that can be solved separately

questions.q: How do you know when to stop decomposing?
questions.a: When each part is small enough to be solved or programmed on its own

stations.name: Why it helps
facts: Smaller problems are easier to understand and to get right.
Different people can work on different parts at the same time.
Each part can be tested on its own, and reused in another program.
stations.challenge: State three advantages of decomposition when programming.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Smaller problems are easier to understand and to get right.
Also credit: Different people can work on different parts at the same time.

questions.q: Which are genuine advantages of decomposition? Select all that apply.
questions.a: Each part can be tested on its own; Several programmers can work at once; Parts can be reused in other programs; Smaller parts are easier to understand

questions.q: A team of five is writing a shop system. How does decomposition help them?
questions.a: Each person takes a separate part, such as payments or stock, and they can work at the same time

stations.name: Structure diagrams
facts: A structure diagram shows the parts of a problem as a tree, from the whole system down.
The top box is the whole problem; each level below breaks the level above into parts.
It is a top-down design: general at the top, detailed at the bottom.
stations.challenge: Draw a structure diagram for a cinema booking system, with three levels.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A structure diagram shows the parts of a problem as a tree, from the whole system down.
Also credit: The top box is the whole problem; each level below breaks the level above into parts.

questions.q: What does a structure diagram show?
questions.a: How a problem breaks down into parts, from the whole system at the top to the detail below

questions.q: Put these levels of a structure diagram for a music app in order, from top to bottom.
questions.a: Music streaming app → Play music, Manage playlists, Search → Add a track, Remove a track, Rename a playlist → Check the track exists, Write it to the playlist file

stations.name: Worked example
facts: A quiz program breaks into: load questions, ask a question, check the answer, keep the score, show the result.
Each of those breaks down further: 'check the answer' needs to compare, mark and give feedback.
The bottom of the diagram is where the code gets written.
stations.challenge: Decompose a program that works out the cost of a pizza order.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A quiz program breaks into: load questions, ask a question, check the answer, keep the score, show the result.
Also credit: Each of those breaks down further: 'check the answer' needs to compare, mark and give feedback.

questions.q: In a quiz program, which level does each part belong to?
questions.a: Quiz program = The whole problem; Ask a question = A main part; Keep the score = A main part; Compare the answer to the correct one = A detailed step; Add one to the score = A detailed step; Print the question text on screen = A detailed step

questions.q: Why is the bottom level of a structure diagram useful to a programmer?
questions.a: Each box there is small enough to be written as a few lines or one subprogram

stations.name: Decomposition and abstraction together
facts: Abstraction decides what matters; decomposition splits what is left into parts.
They are used together on the same problem, usually more than once.
Getting the abstraction wrong means decomposing the wrong problem.
stations.challenge: For a parking app, give one abstraction decision and one decomposition decision.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Abstraction decides what matters; decomposition splits what is left into parts.
Also credit: They are used together on the same problem, usually more than once.

questions.q: Is each decision abstraction or decomposition?
questions.a: Deciding the app does not need the car's colour = Abstraction; Splitting the app into find a space, pay, and extend a stay = Decomposition; Ignoring the driver's age = Abstraction; Separating the payment code from the map code = Decomposition; Storing only the space number, not its exact position = Abstraction; Writing 'check space is free' as its own subprogram = Decomposition

questions.q: Why does abstraction usually come first?
questions.a: You need to know what the problem really is before you can split it into the right parts

stations.name: Answering decomposition questions
facts: Name the sub-problems: vague answers like 'break it into parts' score nothing.
Say why the split helps: testing, reuse, sharing the work, or understanding.
If a structure diagram is asked for, draw levels, not a list.
stations.challenge: Plan a six-mark answer on decomposing a school library system.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Name the sub-problems: vague answers like 'break it into parts' score nothing.
Also credit: Say why the split helps: testing, reuse, sharing the work, or understanding.

questions.q: Which is the strongest exam answer?
questions.a: The system splits into borrow, return, search and fines; each can be written and tested separately, and search can be reused elsewhere

questions.q: A question asks for a structure diagram. What loses marks most often?
questions.a: Writing a list of steps in order instead of a tree of parts

final.name: Final challenge: build the tree

questions.q: Which level of the structure diagram does each item belong to?
questions.a: Takeaway ordering system = Whole system; Browse the menu = Main part; Take payment = Main part; Track the delivery = Main part; Add an item to the basket = Detailed step; Check the card number is 16 digits = Detailed step; Work out the total = Detailed step; Send the driver's position to the app = Detailed step

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
